properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 7 at 2:48AM CDT by NWS North Platte NE
properties.description:
At 248 AM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm near
Bonesteel, or 13 miles northwest of Spencer, moving southeast at 35
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of eastern Boyd
County, including the following locations... Anoka.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 281 between mile markers 210 and 223.
Highway 12 between mile markers 113 and 115, and between mile
markers 118 and 128.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 3:44AM EDT until August 7 at 9:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Central Jackson County in northwestern West Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water. It will take several hours for all the
water from these storms to work through local drainage systems.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 343 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly in the warned area. Between 2 and 3.5 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Ripley and Evans.
- This includes Interstate 77 in West Virginia between mile markers
133 and 140.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Northwestern Randall County in the Panhandle of Texas...

Southwestern Potter County in the Panhandle of Texas...

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to roofs, siding, and trees is possible.
Hail damage to vehicles is expected.

Amarillo and Bushland.
properties.instruction:

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 7 at 2:53AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm...

At 252 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was located
7 nm northeast of Hobe Sound Beach, or 8 nm northeast of Jupiter
Island, moving west to northwest at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.

Frequent cloud to water lightning is occurring with this storm. If
caught on the open water stay below deck and, if possible, avoid
ungrounded metal objects. Remember, lightning can strike beyond 10
miles away from a thunderstorm.
properties.area: Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm; Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 6 at 10:15PM CDT until August 8 at 3:27AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Missouri...

Petite Saline Creek near Boonville affecting Cooper County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Petite Saline Creek near Boonville.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Low lying woodlands and fields near the
creek flood. At 19.5 feet, The creek floods U Highway about 4 miles
southeast of Boonville.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.4 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 6 at 8:04PM CDT until August 8 at 5:43AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Moderate lowland flooding occurs. Hunting
cabins, oil field tanks and pumps are affected, and livestock
become isolated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM CDT Thursday the stage was 16.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
tomorrow afternoon and continue falling below action stage by
late tomorrow.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 12:50pm the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.4 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Wednesday.
-The Yentna River at Lake Creek is forecast to go below flood
stage Saturday morning August 8th.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.




- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
